legend: Given a sequence of integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1 , a_2 , \ldots , a_n$$$ and a prime number x$$$x$$$.

We have a function which takes length$$$length$$$ as a parameter and return the maximum possible value of (ai×ai+1×⋯×ai+length−1)(modx)$$$ (a_i\times a_{i+1}\times \cdots \times a_{i+length-1})\pmod x$$$ , where 1≤i≤(n−length+1)$$$1 \le i \le (n-length+1) $$$.
Your task is to find the smallest length for which this function return maximum possible value.
input: The first line contains a single integer t(1≤t≤105)$$$t (1 \le t \le 10^5)$$$ — the number of test cases in the input. Then t$$$t$$$ test cases follow.

Each query contains two lines. The first line contains two integer n(1≤n≤105)$$$n (1 \le n \le 10^5)$$$: the number of integers in the sequence and x(2≤x≤97)$$$x (2 \le x \le 97)$$$, and the second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,…,an(1≤ai<x)$$$a_1, \ldots ,a_n (1\le a_i  \lt  x)$$$.
It is guaranteed that the total sum of n$$$n$$$ is at most 105$$$10^5$$$ and x$$$x$$$ be a prime number.
output: Print t$$$t$$$ answers to the test cases. Each answer must be consisting of two integers — the maximum possible value of function and the smallest length for which function return maximum possible value.
note: In the first query — Explained in Problem Statement. For length=1$$$length = 1$$$ and 3$$$3$$$, Function return maximum value i.e 4$$$4$$$. We have to return the minimum length i.e 1$$$1$$$.
